## 2. FIRST-GLANCE TEST
A brand-new user sees a slide numbered "49" with a centered white card containing a scatter-plot chart; the chart's title and axis labels are unreadable at this resolution, so the screen's purpose cannot be parsed without study. It appears to offer no actions (static slide). Given the injected VIEW purpose (SVM/kernels/QP lecture frame), the focal point should be the chart/data relationship, but no element wins the eye — the plot is evenly weighted with no title hierarchy or highlight.

- The overall frame is clean and uncluttered with clear white-card separation from the light-gray page background (top bar area / page frame).
- The chart body fills its panel generously with ample breathing room around the four point clusters (chart body, center of panel).

## 5. TOP 3
1. Slide title and chart axis labels are unreadable at this resolution (section 4, first two defect lines) — the viewer cannot tell what the chart shows, which defeats the entire purpose of a lecture slide.
2. The "49" badge is isolated with no slide title or section anchor (section 4, badge defect line) — the slide lacks any framing context for a first-time viewer.

- Whether the four point clusters represent SVM classes, kernel boundaries, or QP regions cannot be determined without readable labels.
